bindings.name: old_holder_commitment
bindings.source: envelope:holderBinding.commitment - a rebind is presented under the holder's current (old) identity, so this MUST equal the envelope holder binding. It is also the holder commitment inside the issuer-signed transcript, so the issuer signature only verifies for the holder the credential was actually issued to.

bindings.name: new_holder_commitment
bindings.justification: The migration target is chosen by the holder: no request-side expected value exists for a commitment freshly derived from a new binding key. In-circuit it is derived from that key and asserted distinct from the old commitment, and it is committed by claim_binding. The verifier defensively re-checks new != old.

bindings.name: credential_id
bindings.justification: Authenticated in-circuit, not request-expected: credential_id is inside the issuer-signed zkc:attestation:credential-rebind:v1 transcript the circuit recomputes and verifies, and the same value is proven a live member of the issuer's non-revocation accumulator. The verifier request vocabulary carries no credentialId expectation, so there is no request-side value to compare it against. A consumer acting on the rebind (an issuer updating its binding record) MUST still match it against its own records for the credential being rebound.

bindings.name: issuer_id_hash
bindings.source: policy:issuerAllowlist - MUST equal string_to_field(issuerId) of the trust-policy issuer matched by the exact (x, y) public key, so the credential's authenticated issuer identity and the key that signed the rebind attestation are the same party the verifier trusts for this proof type. The value is additionally inside the issuer-signed transcript recomputed in-circuit.

bindings.name: schema_id_hash
bindings.justification: Authenticated in-circuit by the issuer signature over the recomputed rebind-attestation transcript, so unlike the deprecated rebind statements this value is issuer-attested rather than prover-chosen. It stays free because a verifier need not care which credential schema was rebound; when it does, the optional pin below applies.
bindings.note: A request MAY pin the expected schema via the schemaIdHash parameter; a supplied pin MUST be equality-checked AFTER cryptographic issuer authentication and only narrows acceptance. It is a filter, never the source of the schema's authenticity.

bindings.name: proof_context
bindings.source: context:value - MUST equal the authenticated request context hash for this presentation.

bindings.name: timestamp
bindings.source: context:timestamp - MUST equal the authenticated request context timestamp, and the issuer-signed validity window MUST contain it.

bindings.name: claim_binding
bindings.note: compute_claim_binding_3 over the rebind public values; the verifier MUST recompute it so the public holders/credential/context cannot be swapped under a stale binding.

bindings.name: accumulator_root
bindings.source: policy:accumulatorState.roots[accumulatorEpoch] - MUST be the root the verifier's AUTHENTICATED (metadata-v2 announcement-chain) accumulator state records for the claimed epoch of the proof's issuer. A prover-supplied root is never revocation authentication.

bindings.name: accumulator_epoch
bindings.source: policy:accumulatorState - MUST NOT lag the verifier's current epoch view by more than the tighter of the policy and announcement epoch-lag bounds, and MUST NOT be ahead of that view.

bindings.name: current_epoch
bindings.source: policy:accumulatorState.currentEpoch - MUST equal the verifier's own current accumulator epoch view for the proof's issuer.

bindings.name: issuer_public_key_x
bindings.source: policy:issuerAllowlist - the (x, y) key MUST be an exact member of the verifier trust policy's issuer allowlist, and the matched issuer MUST be trusted for this proof type.

bindings.name: issuer_public_key_y
bindings.source: policy:issuerAllowlist - checked together with issuer_public_key_x as one exact allowlist key.
